title: Criminology, B.S. (College of the Liberal Arts)
notes: Structurally identical to the 2022-23 and 2023-24 editions (see CRIMBS-2022.json / CRIMBS-2023.json), verified by fetching this year's archive page directly (raw HTML, not just WebFetch's summary, per the known confabulation risk on archive.psu.edu pages -- cross-checked the printed semester subtotals against the page's own 'Total Credits 121'): same 121-credit total (no LA 83 First-Year Seminar or LA 283 Second-Year Seminar -- those first appear starting with the 2025-26 edition, see CRIMBS-2025.json / CRIMBS-2026.json's own notes), same Common Requirements for the Major (CRIM/CRIMJ/SOC 12, CRIM/CRIMJ 100, CRIM 249, CRIM 250W, STAT 200), same four Options with identical course lists for the Computing and Statistics option this plan models (SOC 470, STAT 480, and the 16cr CAS 483/CMPSC 203/MATH 110+111 or 140+141/MIS 204/STAT 460/462/464 list), and the same 'CRIM 12/SOC 12 -> CRIM 249 -> CRIM 250W' Critical Sequencing Note. Real, purely textual differences found on this year's own archive page versus 2023-24 (none affecting course lists, credits, or sequencing): LST 370 ('Research Methods for Law and Government Information Resources') was dropped from the Legal Studies option's course list -- irrelevant here since this plan models the Computing and Statistics option -- and one course title in the shared Race/Ethnicity/Gender list changed from CAS 455 'Gender Roles in Communication' to 'Topics in Gender and Communication' (a title-only change, same course code). This plan is built the same way as CRIMBS-2026.json (its own base curriculum, minus the two seminars): the LA 83 item is removed from Semester 1 (target_credits reduced 13.5 -> 12) and the 'Second-Year Liberal Arts Seminar' slot is removed from Semester 4 (target_credits reduced 16.5 -> 15), and 'LA' is dropped from departments (no LA course appears anywhere else in this plan), mirroring the identical LA-department-only-since-2025 pattern already established in CRIM-2022.json/CRIM-2023.json/CRIM-2024.json for the sibling B.A. Every real hidden-prereq gap documented in CRIMBS-2026.json's own notes (the MATH 3 -> MATH 4 -> MATH 21 -> STAT 200 chain, the SOC 207 -> SOC 470 chain, the checksheet's MATH 140/141 mandatory-calculus-pair addition, and the shared crim_catalog.json CRIM 249/CRIM 250W empty-prereq_groups gap) applies identically this year -- these are stable course-description-level facts, not something that changed between catalog editions, confirmed by the CRIM-2022/2023/2024.json siblings finding the identical MATH-chain gap in their own archive fetches. Race/Ethnicity/Gender and 4XX CRIM Core-vs-Non-Core match patterns are reused from CRIMBS-2026.json's own department-checksheet-sourced lists for the same reason given in CRIM-2022.json's notes: no bulletin edition checked (2022-23 through the live 2026-27 page) publishes the list content on the program page itself, only a generic 'from list' pointer -- this is an inherited assumption, not independently re-verified for this specific year.
